case_name: Manmohan Singh Jaitla and another v The Commissioner. Union Territory Chandigarh And Ors. Etc.
facts: Guru Nanak Khalsa High School, an aided school, dispensed with the service of Headmaster Manmohan Singh Jaitla and Drawing Teacher Amir Singh claiming to exercise power under an agreement executed by each of them with the management of the school.

The school receives 95% of its expenses as grant from the Government and for contribution 5% of the expenses claims thoroughly arbitrary powers to be presently pointed out which appears to be anachronistic.
Manmohan Singh Jaitla was appointed as Headmaster on March 28, 1976 and confirmed with effect from May 1, 1977.
Amir Singh was appointed as Drawing Teacher on March 21, 1976.
The Managing Committee of the school informed Manmohan Singh Jaitla that his services were no longer required with effect from January 31, 1983.
The Managing Committee of the school terminated Amir Singh's service on February 28, 1983.
Manmohan Singh Jaitla and Amir Singh approached the Deputy Commissioner and Commissioner without success.
They filed a petition under Art. 32 of the Constitution.
issues: Whether the agreement between the teachers and the management of the school can be used to circumvent the mandatory provisions of Sec. 3 of the 1969 Act.
Whether the termination of service was malafide and in violation of the statutory provisions.
Whether the Deputy Commissioner and Commissioner have a duty to examine the allegations of malafide and the true nature and character of the impugned order.
petitioner_arguments: The agreement between the teachers and the management of the school cannot be used to circumvent the mandatory provisions of Sec. 3 of the 1969 Act.
The termination of service was not in accordance with the statutory provisions and was malafide.
The Deputy Commissioner and Commissioner have a duty to examine the allegations of malafide and the true nature and character of the impugned order.
respondent_arguments: The agreement between the teachers and the management of the school can be used to circumvent the mandatory provisions of Sec. 3 of the 1969 Act.
The termination of service was in accordance with the statutory provisions and was not malafide.
The Deputy Commissioner and Commissioner do not have a duty to examine the allegations of malafide and the true nature and character of the impugned order.
court_reasoning: The court held that the agreement between the teachers and the management of the school cannot be used to circumvent the mandatory provisions of Sec. 3 of the 1969 Act.
The court found that the termination of service was malafide and in violation of the statutory provisions.

The court emphasized the importance of ensuring that the statutory provisions are complied with and that the Deputy Commissioner and Commissioner have a duty to examine the allegations of malafide and the true nature and character of the impugned order.
holding: The order of termination of service is bad and ab initio void.
The court granted relief to Manmohan Singh Jaitla and Amir Singh by setting aside the order of termination of their services.
cases_cited: Manmohan Singh Jaitla and another v The Commissioner
